answer:
Final natural-language hypothesis (public submission):

"Summed social capital — defined as the z-score sum of Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU), Amber (Zamber) and Monument Count (ZMonument) — peaked in the 14th century BCE, anchored at BCE 1400 / CE −1400 / ≈3350 calBP (the 100-year unit BCE 1400–1301, dataset group OBA = older Bronze Age): the capital.csv century row BCE 1400 sums to 4.238 (2.540 + (−0.010) + 1.708), and the independent interpolated time-series century bin CE −1400 gives the identical 4.238, confirming the peak. This peak sits on a high plateau: the BCE 1300 row carries the same maximum value, and BCE 1200/1100 (3.622) is the close second. At the peak century, the components that increase relative to the immediately preceding century (BCE 1500) are, ranked by magnitude: Copper & Gold (+2.90, from −0.36 to +2.54), Monument Count (+1.54, from +0.17 to +1.71), and Amber only marginally (+0.14, from −0.15 to −0.01; amber stays below its own long-run mean, so it is not an 'elevated' capital component at the peak). The peak is therefore driven primarily by copper/gold wealth and monumental construction, i.e., elite material display and monument building in the OBA phase, while amber contributes negligibly to the rise."

Workflow: (1) read all three datasets, fixing decimal-comma numerics; (2) define social capital = ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument; (3) main analysis on capital.csv (one row = one 100-yr century unit): rank rows by summed social, peak at BCE 1400; (4) cross-validation on time_series_data.csv interpolated columns (CopperGold_inter+Amber_inter+MonumentCount_inter) binned by CE//100×100: peak bin −1400 (= BCE 1400), matching; (5) component 'increase' under main criterion (peak vs preceding century), aux criteria (vs series mean; 5-century trajectory); (6) sensitivity adding one extra indicator at a time and all 12 z-variables. Reproducible script: analysis_social_capital.py (executed, output analysis_output.txt).

Honest caveats: (a) adding Depot (ZHort) or HouseSize or PotteryForm to the sum moves the peak to 1100/1200/2700 BCE respectively (those indicators peak elsewhere), while MonumentSize/Sickle/AxesCelts/PotteryDecoration keep the 1400 BCE peak and the all-12-variable aggregate also peaks at 1400 BCE — so the result is definition-specific but robust under the capital triad and under the full 12-variable sum; (b) amber "increases" only under the previous-century-delta criterion, not under the above-series-mean criterion (marginal, −0.01 vs mean ≈ 0); (c) century naming is ambiguous: BCE 1400–1301 = 14th century BCE under the standard block convention, but the informal "1400s BCE / 15th century" label also exists — hence the numeric anchors BCE 1400 / CE −1400 / calBP ≈3350 are reported first.
